chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:
Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Guard your books carefully, for you will soon have need of them.'

key_terms.احْتَفِظُوا: Guard/preserve — a direct plural imperative commanding the careful safekeeping of written hadith
key_terms.كُتُبِكُمْ: Your books — the written collections of hadith and Islamic knowledge in the companions' possession

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say about preserving hadith books according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) commands his companions to preserve their written collections of hadith. The forward-looking urgency of سَوْفَ تَحْتَاجُونَ ('you will soon need them') anticipates a future time of tribulation — widely understood by Shia scholars as a reference to the period of occultation (ghaybah) — when written records would be the only reliable safeguard of authentic teachings.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Be preserving with your books, for very soon you would need those’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from ’Ubayd ibn Zurara who has said the following.
“Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said, ‘You must preserve your books because you will soon need them.’”
